note: Static explainers for Macro Engine pillars, keyed by engine row id. Content: Hercules (COLLAB.md spec, 2026-10-08). Update `live` as conditions change.

fiscal.body: Deficits, debt sustainability, sovereign spreads. Funds stress leaks into the currency.
fiscal.live: US: Democrats sweep the midterms — AP called the Senate, NBC/CBS project the House — divided government into 2027 caps the fiscal-expansion path; yields + DXY fell in Asia on the result. UK: Healey's first Budget DELIVERED Oct 28 — headroom £15B in 2029/30 (vs £23.6B March), OBR 2027 growth cut to 1.0%. France: Moody's SPARED France (Aa3 affirmed, negative outlook).
fiscal.title: Fiscal & sovereign risk

growth.body: Who is accelerating, who is stalling (GDP, jobs, PMIs). Always comparative. Stronger growth pulls in capital and raises hike expectations.
growth.live: US Q3 GDP advance BEAT: 3.4% SAAR (vs 3.2% consensus, prev 2.2%); JOLTS BEAT 7.523M + factory orders BEAT +1.8% Nov 3; claims 194K. NZ Q3 jobs MISS Nov 3: employment -0.1% (vs +0.4% fcst), unemployment 5.7% (vs 5.5%) — the week's big NZ print went the wrong way. EZ Q3 GDP BEAT (+0.4% q/q vs 0.2% fcst) but France CONTRACTED (-0.1%).
growth.title: Growth differentials

inflation.body: CPI/PCE vs the central bank's target. High inflation alone strengthens nothing — what matters is what the bank does about it.
inflation.live: US Sep PCE in line: headline +0.5% m/m, +3.6% y/y; core +0.3% m/m, +3.1% y/y. Swiss CPI BEAT Nov 3: +0.2% m/m, 1.5% y/y (vs 1.3% fcst). Nov 4: EZ flash CPI PRINTED inline at 4.0% (prev 3.8%, a three-year high, energy 20.8% y/y), core steady 2.5% (Reuters/Eurostat) — December ECB hike case intact, no fresh impulse. AU Q3 CPI hotter than the RBA's path (trimmed 3.7% y/y).
inflation.title: Inflation

policy.body: Central banks moving in different directions. It is the gap between them that moves currencies: money flows toward higher rates.
policy.live: FOMC HELD Oct 28 at 3.75-4.00% (10-2; Cook + Hammack for a hike) — December hike ~78.9% Nov 3 (CME FedWatch) after the JOLTS + factory orders beats, ~82% Nov 4 morning (TradingKey/CME FedWatch). RBA HIKED Nov 3 to 4.85% (6-3, fifth hike of 2026). BoE Thu Nov 5: hike ~96.7% to 4.00% (Morningstar derivatives; first since Aug 2023). ECB HELD Oct 29 at 2.50% — Dec 17 hike all but certain per Reuters sources.
policy.title: Policy divergence

positioning.body: Where speculators already stand (CFTC COT, Fridays). When nearly everyone has made the same bet, it can unwind fast: if everyone is long dollars, nobody is left to buy. The contrarian lens — where would a surprise hurt most.
positioning.live: Oct 27 CFTC (released Oct 30): euro net short at a 3-yr low (non-commercial -143,894; contrarian +1 — squeeze side up); yen longs at the 98th percentile (contrarian -1); AUD/NZD shorts at 1st-percentile extremes (contrarian +1 each); GBP shorts at the 5th percentile (contrarian +1); CAD read is population-mixed, held neutral. Scores moved: GBP 3->4, JPY -1->-2, AUD 2->3, NZD 3->4.
positioning.title: Positioning

risk.body: Risk-on vs risk-off. Fear bids USD, JPY, CHF (havens) and sells AUD, NZD, GBP (risk proxies).
risk.live: Asia risk-off on the midterm sweep: Nikkei -3.6% to 60,835 (lowest since early May), Nasdaq futures -1.8%, S&P futures -0.8% — but the haven bid went to JPY/CHF (USD/JPY ~157.63 Asia low, USD/CHF ~0.8145), not the dollar; DXY fell to a one-month low (~101.45). Europe morning: equities turned higher (STOXX 600 +0.5%, MSCI All-World +0.13% — Reuters) and the dollar steadied (DXY ~101.39, USD/JPY back to ~158.43).
risk.title: Risk sentiment

tot.body: Export prices vs import prices: oil, metals. The same price moves two currencies opposite ways — say which and why.
tot.live: Brent ~$104.36 / WTI ~$96.72 Europe morning Nov 4 (Reuters, 0730 GMT — up ~0.7% after an early dip on US-Iran war/diplomacy uncertainty after the midterm sweep); spread ~$7.64. API drew -5.267M bbl (vs a small expected draw); EIA due today 9:30am CT. Net importers (EUR/JPY) get relief; exporters (CAD/AUD) lose tailwind.
tot.title: Terms of trade
